page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.large is a burstable compute-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8488C processor operating at 3.2 GHz, configured with 1 physical core and 2 virtual CPUs. Memory allocation consists of 4.0 GB of DDR5 RAM rated at 5 GHz, providing a compute-oriented 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware-assisted acceleration flags are present, including AVX-512, AMX-INT8, and AMX-TILE instruction sets. The server profile includes no local storage and no dedicated baseline network bandwidth, relying on network-attached options for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear bifurcation between single-threaded efficiency and parallel capacity. In single-core testing, the Intel Xeon architecture delivers strong results, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2067.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 33.49 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics reflect the constrained physical execution resources of a single dual-threaded core. The Geekbench multi-core score registers at 2547.0, and multi-core stress-ng CPU performance sits in the bottom 10 percent at 2086.47. Uncached memory bandwidth tests for both reads and writes hovered between 13.13 GB/sec and 14.34 GB/sec, placing the memory subsystem in the lowest tiers for high-throughput streaming.

From an architectural standpoint, the burstable CPU allocation provides qualitative cost advantages for low-duty workloads that prioritize modern CPU instruction support without demanding sustained multi-core saturation. However, the absence of local disks and constrained memory bandwidth make it unsuitable for high-throughput transactional databases or high-volume static web serving. The c7i-flex.large is primarily fitted for lightweight web services, continuous integration build runners, microservices, and general background tasks that benefit from burstable clock speed and modern vector instructions.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.large is a compute-optimized, burstable instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8488C x86_64 processor clocked at 3.2 GHz, providing 2 vCPUs from a single physical core with hyperthreading, alongside 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory. The hardware configuration lacks bundled local storage and includes no dedicated baseline network bandwidth, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Instruction sets include AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-threaded CPU execution and compression throughput, contrasted with poor multi-core and uncached memory bandwidth scores due to core count limitations. This resource balance makes the instance cost-efficient for intermittent processing needs, lightweight microservices, small CI/CD tasks, and low-traffic applications that do not require continuous multi-threaded compute or high data throughput.
